title: Balanced Relay
statement: A relay station receives a signal made entirely of bracket symbols. Every opening bracket must be closed by the same bracket type, and inner groups must close before outer groups. Decide whether the entire signal is balanced. An empty signal is balanced.
constraints: 0 ≤ signal length ≤ 200,000. Every symbol is one of ( ) [ ] { }.
outputFormat: Return BALANCED if all groups close correctly; otherwise return BROKEN.

title: Signal Window
statement: Your receiver keeps a contiguous window of an incoming signal. A window is clear when no symbol occurs twice inside it. Find the greatest length of any clear window. You may discard symbols only from the ends of a window; you cannot rearrange the signal.
constraints: 0 ≤ signal length ≤ 200,000. Symbols are lowercase English letters a–z or digits 0–9.
outputFormat: Return the maximum clear-window length as one integer. For an empty signal, return 0.

title: Cargo Pairs
statement: A cargo dispatcher has n numbered crates, each with an integer balance weight. Two different crates may share a carrier when their weights add to target. Count every unordered pair of crate positions that can share a carrier. A crate can appear in several candidate pairs; you are counting possibilities, not assigning carriers. Equal weights at different positions still represent different crates.
inputFormat: Arguments: weights (int[]), target (long). n is weights.length.
outputFormat: Return the number of unordered pairs (i, j) with i < j and weight[i] + weight[j] = target.

title: Coverage Line
statement: A maintenance drone paints several stretches of a straight rail. Stretch [a, b) includes a and stops just before b. Overlapping paint counts only once. Find the total rail length covered after all stretches have been painted; their arrival order has no significance.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; −10^12 ≤ a < b ≤ 10^12. Endpoints are integers. Use a 64-bit answer.
inputFormat: Arguments: intervals (long[][]). Each interval is [start, end]; touching intervals may be merged.
outputFormat: Return the total covered length.

title: Dock Slots
statement: Delivery pods reserve one docking slot from their arrival time up to, but excluding, their departure time. A slot can be reused exactly when its previous pod departs. Determine the smallest number of slots that lets every reservation proceed without waiting.
inputFormat: Arguments: reservations (int[][]). Each reservation is [arrival, departure]. A departing ship frees its slot at that time.
outputFormat: Return the minimum number of slots. With no reservations, return 0.

title: Grid Courier
statement: A courier starts in the top-left cell of a rectangular warehouse and must reach the bottom-right cell. Each move enters a horizontally or vertically adjacent open cell. Walls cannot be crossed. Find the fewest moves; a blocked start or destination makes the route impossible.
constraints: 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 500. A dot is an open cell and # is a wall.
outputFormat: Return the fewest moves, or -1 if no route exists.

title: Target Bursts
statement: A sensor reports signed adjustments in chronological order. A burst is a nonempty contiguous sequence of reports. Count the bursts whose adjustments add to the requested target. Negative adjustments are valid, and bursts may overlap.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; |adjustment| ≤ 1,000,000; |target| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The count needs 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: values (int[]), target (long). n is values.length.
outputFormat: Return the number of target-sum bursts.

title: Compass Picks
statement: A survey team can visit k of its numbered stations. Choose those closest to the origin. Compare squared Euclidean distance; when two stations are equally distant, the smaller original station number comes first. Report the chosen station numbers in that order.
constraints: 0 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |x|, |y| ≤ 1,000,000. Station numbers are 1-based. Use 64-bit squared distances.
inputFormat: Arguments: points (int[][]), k (int). Each point is [x, y]. Return the 1-based positions of the k selected points.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Token Mint
statement: A workshop has unlimited tokens in the listed positive denominations. Assemble exactly the requested value using as few tokens as possible. A denomination can be reused; if exact assembly is impossible, report failure.
constraints: 0 ≤ denomination count ≤ 100; 0 ≤ target ≤ 100,000; distinct denominations are between 1 and 10,000.
inputFormat: Arguments: coins (int[]), target (int). n is coins.length.
outputFormat: Return the minimum token count, or -1 when impossible. Value 0 requires no tokens.

title: Rising Antennas
statement: Antennas stand in a fixed line. Select some of them without changing their order so that each selected height is strictly greater than the previous selected height. Skipping antennas is allowed. Find the greatest possible number selected.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; heights are signed 32-bit integers. Equal heights cannot extend a strictly rising sequence.
outputFormat: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Archive Lookup
statement: An archive stores nondecreasing integer keys, including duplicates. For each query, find the first position whose stored key is at least the requested key. Positions are zero-based. A query beyond every stored key has no answer.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; 1 ≤ queries ≤ 200,000; keys and requests are signed 32-bit integers.
inputFormat: Arguments: keys (int[]), queries (int[]). n and m are the lengths of the first and second arrays. keys is sorted. Return the first 1-based position of each query, or -1 if absent.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Island Ledger
statement: A coastal chart marks land as 1 and water as 0. Land cells belong to the same island when a chain of horizontal or vertical land neighbors connects them. Diagonal contact alone does not connect islands. Count the islands and measure the largest one.
constraints: 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 500. An island size is its number of land cells.
outputFormat: Return [islandCount, largestIslandSize]. An all-water map returns [0, 0].

title: Turned Ledger
statement: A ledger originally listed distinct keys in increasing order. Someone moved a possibly empty prefix to the end, preserving the order inside both parts. Locate the smallest key in the resulting list. The list may already be sorted.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000. Keys are distinct signed 32-bit integers. Aim for logarithmic search time.
outputFormat: Return the zero-based position of the smallest key.

title: Equal Banner
statement: A banner is woven from tiles labeled 0 or 1. Choose one contiguous piece containing equally many tiles of each label. Find the longest such piece; you may remove tiles from the ends but cannot reorder or remove tiles inside the piece.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000. Each tile is 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Return the greatest balanced-piece length, or 0 if no nonempty piece qualifies.

title: Step Bridges
statement: Stepping stones are numbered 0 through n. Start on stone 0 and reach stone n using jumps of exactly one or two positions. Some positive-numbered stones are broken and cannot be landed on. Count distinct sequences of jumps; crossing over a broken stone is allowed.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; broken indices are distinct and between 1 and n. Stone 0 is never broken.
inputFormat: Arguments: n (int), broken (int[]). n is the destination step. broken lists the step numbers that cannot be used.
outputFormat: Return the number of routes modulo 1,000,000,007. When n is 0 there is one empty route.

title: Two Sum
statement: Find two different positions in an array whose values add to the target. If several pairs work, choose the smallest first position, then the smallest second position. Positions start at 1 and the first position must be smaller than the second.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), target (long). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the 1-based pair [i, j], with i < j and the smallest first position, then second position. Return [] if no pair exists.

title: Palindrome Check
statement: Check whether a string reads the same from left to right and from right to left. Compare every character exactly as written. The empty string is a palindrome.
constraints: 0 ≤ string length ≤ 200,000. Characters are lowercase English letters or digits.
outputFormat: Return true for a palindrome, otherwise false.

title: Valid Anagram
statement: Decide whether the second string can be made by rearranging all characters of the first. Every character must be used exactly once, so repeated letters must have the same counts.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 200,000 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return true if the strings are anagrams, otherwise false.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement: An array gives a stock price for each day. You may buy once and sell on a later day. Find the largest possible profit. You may also make no trade, for a profit of zero.
outputFormat: Return the maximum profit.

title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Check whether any value appears at least twice in an array. Equal values at different positions count as a duplicate.
outputFormat: Return true if a duplicate exists, otherwise false.

title: Missing Number
statement: An array contains n different numbers chosen from 0 through n. Exactly one number in that range is absent. Find it. The array is not necessarily sorted.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000. All given numbers are distinct and between 0 and n.
outputFormat: Return the missing number.

title: Move Zeroes
statement: Move every zero to the end of the array while keeping the original order of all nonzero values. Return the resulting array, including every zero.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Single Number
statement: Exactly one array value appears once. Every other distinct value appears exactly twice. Find the value that appears once. Aim for linear time and constant extra space.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 99,999; n is odd; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The stated occurrence counts are guaranteed.
outputFormat: Return the value that occurs once.

title: Majority Element
statement: Find the value that appears in more than half of the array positions. Such a value is guaranteed to exist. Aim for linear time and constant extra space.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. One value occurs more than n / 2 times.
outputFormat: Return the majority value.

title: Range Sum Query
statement: Answer sum queries on an array that never changes. Each query names an inclusive range of positions. Positions start at 1. Preprocess the array so that each query can be answered quickly.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, q ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000; 1 ≤ left ≤ right ≤ n. Sums may need 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), queries (int[][]). Each query is [left, right], using inclusive 1-based positions in nums.
outputFormat: Return one sum for each inclusive 1-based query, keeping the query order.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Find the greatest common divisor and least common multiple of two positive integers. The greatest common divisor divides both numbers; the least common multiple is the smallest positive number divisible by both.
constraints: 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 1,000,000,000. The least common multiple may need a 64-bit integer.
outputFormat: Return [greatestCommonDivisor, leastCommonMultiple] as a long[].

title: Merge Sorted Arrays
statement: Merge two arrays that are already sorted in nondecreasing order. Keep all values, including duplicates, and return them in nondecreasing order. Aim for linear time in the combined length.
constraints: 0 ≤ n, m ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. Both input arrays are sorted.
inputFormat: Arguments: first (int[]), second (int[]). n and m are the lengths of the first and second arrays.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Maximum Subarray
statement: Find the largest sum of a nonempty contiguous part of an array. The chosen part must contain at least one value, including when every value is negative.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The answer may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the maximum subarray sum.

title: Next Permutation
statement: Rearrange the array into the next lexicographically greater ordering of its values. Compare arrays at the first position where they differ. If no greater ordering exists, return the smallest ordering. Repeated values are allowed.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. Aim for linear time and constant extra space.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Container With Most Water
statement: Vertical lines stand one unit apart. Choose two lines to form the sides of a container. Its width is the distance between their positions and its height is the shorter line. Find the largest possible area. Lines between the chosen sides do not affect the area.
constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ height ≤ 1,000,000,000. The area may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the maximum container area.

title: Daily Temperatures
statement: For each day, find how many days you must wait for a strictly warmer temperature. Equal temperatures do not count as warmer. If there is no later warmer day, use zero.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; −50 ≤ temperature ≤ 100. Aim for linear time.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A strictly increasing array was rotated by moving a possibly empty prefix to the end. Find the target in the rotated array. All values are distinct. Aim for logarithmic search time.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; values and target are between −1,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), target (int). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the zero-based position of the target, or -1 when absent.

title: Jump Game
statement: Start at the first array position. A value tells you the maximum number of positions you may jump forward from there; shorter positive jumps are allowed. Decide whether you can reach the last position. A one-element array is already at the destination.
outputFormat: Return true if the last position is reachable, otherwise false.

title: House Robber
statement: Each house in a straight row contains the given amount of money. Choose houses to rob without choosing two adjacent houses. Find the largest total you can collect. Choosing no houses is allowed.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ amount ≤ 1,000,000,000. The total may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the maximum total.

title: Word Break
statement: Decide whether the entire string can be split into one or more dictionary words. You may reuse a word as often as needed. An empty string needs no words and always succeeds.
constraints: 0 ≤ string length ≤ 2,000; 0 ≤ dictionary size ≤ 500; each word has 1 to 20 lowercase English letters. The string also uses lowercase English letters. Dictionary words are distinct.
inputFormat: Arguments: text (String), words (String[]). words is the dictionary; a dictionary word may be used more than once.
outputFormat: Return true if a complete split is possible, otherwise false.

title: Edit Distance
statement: Turn the first string into the second using as few edits as possible. One edit inserts a character, deletes a character, or replaces one character. Every edit costs one.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 1,500 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the minimum number of edits.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Find the length of the longest sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same order. Characters may be skipped, but the remaining characters cannot be rearranged. The empty sequence has length zero.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 2,000 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the longest common subsequence length.

title: Shortest Path
statement: Find the cheapest route from the source vertex to the target in a directed weighted graph. Edge weights are nonnegative. You may follow an edge only in its listed direction. Parallel edges and self-loops are allowed.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ m ≤ 200,000; vertices are numbered 1 through n; 0 ≤ edge weight ≤ 1,000,000,000. Route costs may need 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: n (int), edges (int[][]), source (int), target (int). n is the vertex count. Each directed edge is [from, to, weight]. Vertices, source, and target are numbered from 1.
outputFormat: Return the cheapest route cost, or -1 if unreachable. If source equals target, return 0.

title: Course Schedule
statement: You want to finish every course. A prerequisite pair a b means course a must be completed before course b. Decide whether any valid order exists. Separate groups of courses are allowed, but a prerequisite cycle makes completion impossible.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ m ≤ 200,000; course numbers are 1 through n. Repeated pairs and self-prerequisites may appear.
inputFormat: Arguments: n (int), prerequisites (int[][]). n is the course count. Each prerequisite is [before, after], with courses numbered from 1.
outputFormat: Return true if every course can be completed, otherwise false.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Bars of width one form a height map. After it rains, water can remain above lower bars when taller bars hold it on both sides. Find the total amount of trapped water. Water can escape through either end.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ height ≤ 1,000,000,000. The total may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the total trapped water.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: Slide a window of exactly k consecutive positions across the array, starting at the first position and moving one position at a time. Report the largest value in every window. Aim for linear total time.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), k (int). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
statement: A histogram has adjacent bars of width one. Find the largest rectangle that fits entirely under the bars. The rectangle must have a horizontal top and cover a contiguous range of bars. An empty histogram has area zero.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ height ≤ 1,000,000,000. The area may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the largest rectangle area.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
statement: Find the length of the longest contiguous part of a parentheses string that is balanced. A balanced part pairs every opening parenthesis with a later closing parenthesis, with groups closing in the proper order.
constraints: 0 ≤ string length ≤ 200,000. Every character is ( or ).
outputFormat: Return the longest balanced substring length, or 0 if no nonempty substring is balanced.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree
statement: Connect every vertex of an undirected weighted graph using edges with the smallest possible total weight. The chosen edges must form a tree, with no cycles. Negative weights, parallel edges, and self-loops may appear. A self-loop cannot help connect different vertices.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ m ≤ 200,000; vertices are numbered 1 through n; |edge weight| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The total may need 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: n (int), edges (int[][]). n is the vertex count. Each undirected edge is [from, to, weight], with vertices numbered from 1.
outputFormat: Return the total weight as a decimal string, or "IMPOSSIBLE" if the graph is disconnected.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
statement: Choose items to place in a bag with a fixed weight capacity. Each item has a weight and a value, and each item may be taken at most once. Find the largest total value without exceeding the capacity. You do not need to fill the bag exactly.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100; 0 ≤ capacity ≤ 20,000; 1 ≤ item weight ≤ 20,000; 0 ≤ item value ≤ 1,000,000,000. The answer may need 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: weights (int[]), values (int[]), capacity (int). weights[i] and values[i] describe the same item. Both arrays have n items.
outputFormat: Return the maximum obtainable value.

title: Fizz Buzz
statement: List the numbers from 1 through n. Replace multiples of 3 with Fizz, multiples of 5 with Buzz, and multiples of both with FizzBuzz.
outputFormat: Return the n results in order as a String[].

title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
statement: Count the zeros at the end of the decimal representation of n factorial. Do not construct the factorial itself. By definition, 0 factorial is 1.
outputFormat: Return the number of trailing zeros.

title: Count Set Bits
statement: Count how many digits are 1 in the binary representation of a nonnegative integer.
outputFormat: Return the number of set bits.

title: Power of Two
statement: Decide whether n is a power of two, meaning n equals 2 raised to a nonnegative integer power. Zero and negative numbers are not powers of two.
outputFormat: Return true for a power of two, otherwise false.

title: Reverse Integer
statement: Reverse the decimal digits of a signed 32-bit integer, keeping its sign. Leading zeros in the reversed digits disappear. If the result is outside the signed 32-bit range, return zero.
outputFormat: Return the reversed integer, or 0 on overflow.

title: Integer Square Root
statement: Find the largest nonnegative integer whose square is at most n. Return the floor of the square root without relying on floating-point rounding.
outputFormat: Return the integer square root.

title: Excel Column Number
statement: Spreadsheet columns are named A through Z, then AA, AB, and so on. Convert a column name to its 1-based column number. A represents 1 and Z represents 26.
constraints: The name has 1 to 12 uppercase English letters. Use a 64-bit integer.
outputFormat: Return its column number.

title: Roman to Integer
statement: Convert a valid Roman numeral to an integer. I, V, X, L, C, D, and M represent 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, and 1000. In IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, and CM, the smaller symbol is subtracted from the larger one.
constraints: The input is a standard valid Roman numeral representing an integer from 1 through 3999.
outputFormat: Return its integer value.

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement: Find the longest prefix shared by every string in a list. A prefix starts at the first character. If the list is empty or no character is shared at the start, the answer is empty.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200; each string has 0 to 10,000 lowercase English letters; their combined length is at most 200,000.
outputFormat: Return the common prefix, or an empty line when none exists.

title: First Unique Character
statement: Find the first character that appears exactly once in a string. Return its zero-based position.
constraints: 0 ≤ length ≤ 200,000. Characters are lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the first unique character position, or -1 if there is none.

title: Is Subsequence
statement: Decide whether the first string can be obtained by deleting zero or more characters from the second without changing the order of the remaining characters.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 200,000 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return true if the first string is a subsequence of the second, otherwise false.

title: Isomorphic Strings
statement: Decide whether every character in the first string can be consistently replaced to make the second string. Different source characters must map to different destination characters. Character order cannot change.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 200,000 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return true if a one-to-one character mapping exists, otherwise false.

title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
statement: Add all values on the main diagonal and the opposite diagonal of a square matrix. If a cell belongs to both diagonals, count it only once.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The sum may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the sum of the two diagonals without double-counting their intersection.

title: Transpose Matrix
statement: Transpose a matrix by turning each original row into a column. An input with r rows and c columns produces c rows and r columns.
outputFormat: Return the transposed matrix as int[][].

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
statement: Square every value in a nondecreasing array and return the squares in nondecreasing order. Negative values may appear. Aim for linear time.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. Squared values may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the result as long[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Plus One
statement: An array stores a nonnegative decimal integer, one digit per position, most significant digit first. Add one and return the resulting digits. The input has no leading zero unless the number is zero.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10,000; each digit is from 0 through 9.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Add Binary
statement: Add two nonnegative integers written in binary. Return the sum in binary without leading zeros, except that zero is written as 0.
constraints: Each input has 1 to 10,000 binary digits and no unnecessary leading zeros.
outputFormat: Return their binary sum.

title: Ransom Note
statement: Decide whether the first string can be built using letters from the second string. Each occurrence in the second string can be used at most once, and letters may be rearranged.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 200,000 lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return true if the note can be formed, otherwise false.

title: Length of Last Word
statement: Find the number of letters in the last word of text. Words are separated by spaces, and extra spaces may appear at either end. Return 0 if there is no word.
constraints: 0 ≤ line length ≤ 200,000; characters are English letters or spaces.
outputFormat: Return the length of its last word.

title: Pascal's Triangle Row
statement: Return row k of Pascal's triangle, counting the top row [1] as row 0. Each interior value is the sum of the two values above it, and each row begins and ends with 1.
constraints: 0 ≤ k ≤ 60. Values may need 64-bit integers.
outputFormat: Return the result as long[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Three Sum
statement: Count the different value triplets that add to zero. Choose three different array positions, but count a triplet only once regardless of position choices or value order. For example, many zeroes still produce just the triplet (0, 0, 0).
outputFormat: Return the number of distinct zero-sum value triplets.

title: Four Sum Count
statement: Four arrays A, B, C, and D have the same length. Count the index quadruples (i, j, k, l) for which A[i] + B[j] + C[k] + D[l] equals zero. Equal values at different positions count as different choices.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 500; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The answer may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the number of zero-sum index quadruples.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: Find the longest run of consecutive integer values present in an unsorted array. Their positions do not matter. Repeated values cannot extend a run. Aim for linear expected time.
outputFormat: Return the longest consecutive run length.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: For each position, multiply every array value except the value at that position. Do not use division. The product of no values is 1, so a one-element array produces [1]. Aim for linear time.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The absolute product of all nonzero values is at most 10^18; every answer fits a signed 64-bit integer.
outputFormat: Return the result as long[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement: Find the shortest nonempty contiguous part of a positive array whose sum is at least the target. Positive values allow a sliding-window solution.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), target (long). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the minimum length, or 0 if no part qualifies.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement: You may replace at most k characters in a string. Find the greatest length of a contiguous part that can be made entirely of one repeated character.
constraints: 0 ≤ length ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ k ≤ length. Characters are uppercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the greatest achievable repeated-character length.

title: Subarray Product Less Than K
statement: Count nonempty contiguous parts of an array whose product is strictly smaller than k. All array values are positive.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 1 ≤ value ≤ 1,000,000; 0 ≤ k ≤ 10^12. The count may need 64 bits.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), k (long). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the number of qualifying subarrays.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
statement: Decide whether all array positions can be divided into two groups with equal sums. Each position must belong to exactly one group. The groups may be empty, so an empty array succeeds.
outputFormat: Return true if an equal partition exists, otherwise false.

title: Coin Change Combinations
statement: Count the ways to make the target using unlimited coins of the given denominations. Coin order does not matter. For example, 1 + 2 and 2 + 1 are the same combination. The empty choice makes target zero in one way.
constraints: 0 ≤ coin count ≤ 100; 0 ≤ target ≤ 10,000; denominations are distinct integers from 1 through 10,000.
inputFormat: Arguments: coins (int[]), target (int). n is coins.length.
outputFormat: Return the combination count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Unique Paths With Obstacles
statement: Count routes from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell. Every move must go one cell right or one cell down, and walls cannot be entered. A blocked start or destination gives zero routes.
constraints: 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 200. A dot is open and # is a wall.
outputFormat: Return the route count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Minimum Path Sum
statement: Travel from the top-left to the bottom-right of a matrix, moving only right or down. Pay the value of every visited cell, including both ends. Find the smallest total cost.
constraints: 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 300; 0 ≤ cell value ≤ 1,000,000,000. The total may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the minimum path sum.

title: Triangle Minimum Path Sum
statement: Start at the top of a number triangle. From position j in a row, move to position j or j + 1 in the next row. Find the smallest sum from top to bottom, counting every visited number.
constraints: 1 ≤ row count ≤ 400; |value| ≤ 1,000,000. Row i has i values, counting from 1.
outputFormat: Return the minimum path sum.

title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
statement: Start at any cell of the first row of a square matrix and reach the last row. Each move goes down one row and changes the column by -1, 0, or 1, staying inside the matrix. Find the minimum sum of visited cells.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 300; |cell value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. The sum may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the minimum falling path sum.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement: Find the length of the longest contiguous part of a string that reads the same forwards and backwards. Only the length is required, so equally long answers do not need a tie-break.
constraints: 0 ≤ length ≤ 5,000. Characters are lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the longest palindromic substring length.

title: Decode Ways
statement: The numbers 1 through 26 encode the letters A through Z. Count the ways to split a digit string into valid encoded letters. A token cannot begin with zero, so 0 and 06 are invalid while 10 and 20 are valid.
constraints: 1 ≤ length ≤ 100,000. Every character is a decimal digit.
outputFormat: Return the decoding count modulo 1,000,000,007.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement: Evaluate a valid postfix expression. A number pushes a value; an operator consumes the two previous values, with the earlier one on the left. Operators are +, -, *, and /. Integer division truncates toward zero.
constraints: 1 ≤ token count ≤ 100,000; operands are between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000. Every intermediate result fits a signed 64-bit integer. Division by zero never occurs, and the expression leaves exactly one result.
outputFormat: Return the final value.

title: Simplify Unix Path
statement: Simplify an absolute Unix-style path. Repeated slashes act as one slash, . stays in the current directory, and .. moves to the parent. Moving above root stays at root. Other names, including ..., are ordinary directory names.
constraints: 1 ≤ path length ≤ 200,000. The path starts with /. Components use English letters and dots.
outputFormat: Return the canonical path with a single leading slash and no trailing slash unless it is root.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Return the k most frequent distinct array values. Order them by decreasing occurrence count. If two values have the same count, put the smaller value first.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ k ≤ the number of distinct values; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), k (int). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Kth Largest Element
statement: Find the kth largest array value, counting duplicate positions separately. The largest value has rank 1.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), k (int). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the kth largest value.

title: Kth Smallest in a Sorted Matrix
statement: Every row and every column of a square matrix is sorted in nondecreasing order. Find its kth smallest value, counting repeated cells separately.
outputFormat: Return the kth smallest value.

title: Spiral Matrix
statement: Read a matrix in clockwise spiral order. Start at the top-left, move across the top row, then down the right edge, left along the bottom, and up the left edge. Continue inward until every cell is visited once.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Valid Sudoku
statement: Check a partially filled 9 by 9 Sudoku board. Filled digits must not repeat in a row, column, or 3 by 3 box. Empty cells are dots. You only need to check the filled cells, not solve the puzzle or prove that a solution exists.
constraints: Exactly nine rows of nine characters, each a dot or a digit from 1 through 9.
outputFormat: Return true if all filled cells obey the rules, otherwise false.

title: Word Search
statement: Find a word in a character grid. Consecutive letters must be horizontally or vertically adjacent. A grid cell may be used at most once in the same word. The word may start at any cell.
constraints: 1 ≤ rows, columns ≤ 12; 1 ≤ word length ≤ 12. Grid and word use uppercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return true if the word can be traced, otherwise false.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
statement: Remove as few intervals as possible so that none of the remaining intervals overlap. An interval includes its start and excludes its end, so [1, 2) and [2, 3) can both remain.
inputFormat: Arguments: intervals (int[][]). Each interval is [start, end]. Intervals that only touch do not overlap.
outputFormat: Return the minimum number of removed intervals.

title: Task Scheduler
statement: Each task takes one time slot and is identified by an uppercase letter. You may reorder tasks or leave idle slots. Between two executions of the same letter, at least cooldown other slots must pass. Find the fewest slots needed to finish all tasks.
constraints: 0 ≤ task count ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ cooldown ≤ 1,000,000,000. The answer may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the minimum total number of slots.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Find the median of two sorted arrays considered as one sorted sequence. For an even total length, average the two middle values. Aim for logarithmic time rather than merging the full arrays.
constraints: 0 ≤ n, m ≤ 100,000; n + m ≥ 1; |value| ≤ 1,000,000,000. Both arrays are nondecreasing.
inputFormat: Arguments: first (int[]), second (int[]). n and m are the lengths of the first and second arrays.
outputFormat: Return the median as a double.

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Find the shortest contiguous part of the first string containing every character of the second, including repeated occurrences. Matching is case-sensitive. If several shortest windows exist, choose the earliest. An empty target has an empty answer.
constraints: Each string has 0 to 100,000 English letters, uppercase or lowercase.
outputFormat: Return the shortest window, choosing the earliest on ties. Return an empty string if no window exists or the target is empty.

title: Minimum Insertions for a Palindrome
statement: Insert as few characters as possible anywhere in a string so that it becomes a palindrome. You cannot delete, replace, or rearrange existing characters.
constraints: 0 ≤ length ≤ 2,000. Characters are lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the minimum number of insertions.

title: Burst Balloons
statement: Burst every balloon in the best order. Bursting a balloon earns its value times the values of its nearest remaining neighbors. A missing neighbor beyond either end has value 1. After a balloon is removed, its remaining neighbors become adjacent.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200; 0 ≤ balloon value ≤ 1,000. The score may need 64 bits.
outputFormat: Return the greatest total score.

title: Palindrome Partitioning: Minimum Cuts
statement: Cut a string into contiguous pieces so that every piece is a palindrome. Find the smallest number of cuts. A string that is already a palindrome needs zero cuts, as does an empty string.
constraints: 0 ≤ length ≤ 2,000. Characters are lowercase English letters.
outputFormat: Return the minimum cut count.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
statement: Start at any matrix cell and move horizontally or vertically to a strictly larger value. Find the greatest number of cells in such a path. Equal values cannot extend it, and diagonal moves are forbidden.
outputFormat: Return the longest increasing path length.

title: Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K
statement: Find the shortest nonempty contiguous part whose sum is at least the target. Values may be negative, so an ordinary positive-number sliding window is not sufficient.
inputFormat: Arguments: nums (int[]), target (long). n is nums.length.
outputFormat: Return the minimum length, or -1 if no part qualifies.

title: Count Smaller Numbers After Self
statement: For every array position, count how many later positions contain a strictly smaller value. Equal values do not count. Return the counts in the original position order.
outputFormat: Return the result as int[], in the order described above. Return an empty array when there are no results.

title: Stock Profit With Two Transactions
statement: A stock price is given for each day. Make at most two buy-then-sell transactions to maximize profit. You must sell before buying again and may hold at most one share. Making no trade is allowed.
outputFormat: Return the maximum profit with at most two transactions.

title: Regular Expression Matching
statement: Match the entire string against a pattern. A lowercase letter matches itself, a dot matches any single letter, and * means zero or more copies of the preceding letter or dot. Matching only part of the string is not enough.
constraints: String and pattern lengths are 0 to 2,000. The string uses lowercase English letters. The pattern uses lowercase letters, dots, and stars; a star never appears first or immediately after another star.
outputFormat: Return true for a complete match, otherwise false.
